articles.headline: GTA 6’s Worst Feature Needs to Be Patched ASAP
keyFacts: Polygon reported that Grand Theft Auto 6 players are frustrated by the game's clunky, overly sensitive currency slider used for depositing and withdrawing cash at ATMs and stash boxes.
Rockstar Games stated that GTA 6 sold over 32 million copies and generated 3.79 billion dollars in revenue prior to its release.
GTA 6 is currently available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.
body: After years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here. And somehow, miraculously, it's living up to the impossible level of hype surrounding it. Rockstar's game is a staggering technological and artistic achievement in countless ways. The world of Leonida is vast and intricate, and the emergent gameplay enabled by hundreds of unique NPCs is truly astonishing. But there's one thing about GTA 6 I find absolutely infuriating so far, and it's extremely minor: depositing and withdrawing money from Jason's stash box and ATMs is a total pain in the ass.

In the early hours of the game, Jason doesn't have a bank account. (He later tells Lucia he doesn't want to be "in the system.") So while he's making a living doing odd jobs and waiting for Lucia to be released from prison, he's keeping money under the floorboards in his bedroom. In order to select the amount you want to deposit or withdraw from the stash box, you press left or right on the d-pad. It takes forever for the numbers to tick up or down — until suddenly it doesn't, and you've whizzed far past the figure you wanted to input. The sensitivity of the counter is totally out of whack, going from a trickle to a fire hose instantaneously. I figured I was missing something — surely it should not be this difficult to wrangle the stash box?

At first, I generously assumed this was some kind of artistic flourish. Jason isn't counting the cash he places in the stash by hand every time; he's just eyeballing it. Then, about halfway through Chapter 1, you get access to the BuckMe app, essentially a bank account for people with terrible credit like Jason and Lucia. In addition to keeping cash at home, you can now deposit your ill-gotten gains at ATMs throughout Leonida. (Having a BuckMe account also allows you to make more expensive purchases at the gun store.) I assumed my days of wrangling that horrible slider were over. Surely the ATM would feature a numerical keypad, and I could just enter the amount I wanted to deposit or withdraw. After all, a similar interface appears elsewhere in the game, for door codes and lockboxes. Nope! For no discernible reason, ATMs also use the same clunky, left-to-right scrolling interface as the stash box.

Perhaps the intent here is to encourage you to put all your money in your BuckMe and Family Savings account as soon as the option becomes available. But I enjoy having a few hundred dollars of "fuck around money" for buying snacks or car repairs. Yes, you can use the app for most stuff, but I really hate the idea of having to schlep back to the house or find an ATM to get cash. I can't imagine this would be difficult for Rockstar to fix, and I would even tolerate it for the stash box if I must. But there is literally no excuse for an ATM to work this way in a video game in 2026.

I'm not the only one who has beef with this mechanic. Plenty of folks on Reddit have noticed it too. "Ok I’m not the only one I was hoping there was a way to input the exact numbers and I haven’t found it yet but guess not," wrote one user. "Little bit more, little bit more, little bit more, ok and stop.... Fuck, way too much," wrote another.

The horrible banking interface does not appear to have slowed GTA 6's ascent to cultural dominance. The game sold more than 32 million copies during the run-up to release and has already made $3.79 billion in revenue, according to Rockstar Games. GTA 6 is available now on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

body: Sunday's matchup between the Tennessee Titans and the Dallas Cowboys looks poised for high-scoring madness, as the two worst defenses in the league face off.

Dallas tried to reset the issue by stripping first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of play-calling duties , and having senior defensive assistant and veteran coach Mike Pettine call the plays going forward .

articles.headline: Why the Bears will or won't beat the Saints in Week 11
keyFacts: The Chicago Bears play the New Orleans Saints in Week 11 seeking their fifth consecutive win and eighth victory of the season.
The article states the Bears are favored to win due to their strong run game and defense, but warn that turnovers and penalties could cause a loss.
The piece outlines that Chicago can succeed by dominating the line of scrimmage and pressuring Saints quarterback Tyler Shough.
body: The Chicago Bears are looking for their fifth straight win and eighth overall win of the year when they take on the New Orleans Saints. With a win, it would be the second season in a row that Chicago wins the next game after their bye week.

On paper, the Bears have every reason to win this game. They have a successful run game, and are getting a large piece of it back with Kyle Monangai, while the Saints have struggled against the run throughout this season. Chicago’s defense has played well this season, especially after trading for All-Pro Jeffery Simmons. But crazier things have happened. The Bears have already lost once this season when it looked on paper like they should win. So, they cannot take New Orleans lightly.
Here is what it would take for the Bears to win this game and what it would take for Chicago to lose this game to the Saints.
Why the Bears will win

The Bears will win this game because they have a superior offense that is going to put up a lot of points against this struggling defense. New Orleans has already allowed three teams to put up at least 30 points against them, including Chicago’s NFC North rival, the Detroit Lions, back in the season opener. The Bears have proven this season that they are capable of putting up points and especially with Monangai coming back, they should be able to dominate the line of scrimmage and find the end zone multiple times.

Defensively, Chicago will shut down the Saints’ run game and force Tyler Shough to win this game through the air. However, especially as a young quarterback, he is going to make some mistakes, which the Bears can capitalize on. They should also be able to get pressure in the backfield and sack Shough at least a few times.
Why the Bears won’t win

The Bears will not win this game because of penalties and turnovers. Chicago’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers never should have been close, but it was because the Bears turned the ball over five times. While I doubt Chicago will turn it over that many times again, the Saints’ defense could look to force a few turnovers to get momentum on their side and get the win.

Chicago has also struggled with penalties at times throughout the season. They also tend to come at the worst possible time. Self-inflicted wounds like turnovers and penalties are not how winning football teams play and that is the only real way the Bears could lose this game is by defeating themselves.

articles.headline: Spurs 'a match for anyone' as European hopes boosted
keyFacts: Tottenham Hotspur secured a 3-1 away win against Manchester City on Sunday with two late goals.
Manager Martin Ho said the victory proves his team can be a match for anyone.
Tottenham sit fifth in the Women's Super League table, three points behind the final European place.
body: - Published
Dreams of reaching the Women's Champions League may have seemed fanciful for Tottenham Hotspur when the season began.
The Women's Super League has an established big four, and big-spending London City Lionesses were the side making the most obvious play to disrupt that dominance.
But a hugely impressive and deserved win at Manchester City on Sunday afternoon proves Spurs are a team on the up, and the table shows they remain firmly in top-three contention.
Two late goals secured a 3-1 win at Joie Stadium, but this was no smash-and-grab job. Spurs were more dynamic than sluggish City, pressing them into submission.
They restricted their hosts' stellar attack to precious few chances and took the ones they created.
"When we are on our game, we can be a match for anyone," Spurs manager Martin Ho said in his post-match media conference.
"It gives us confidence - but it is just one game."
Victory kept Spurs, whose highest finish in the WSL is fifth, firmly in the mix this time.
They are fifth again, but just three points behind London City Lionesses who occupy the final European place as the league heads into a last international break of 2026.
Chelsea lead the way from Manchester City, with Manchester United one point ahead of Tottenham, who in turn sit handily clear of their sixth-placed north London rivals Arsenal.
The big four are therefore all present in the top six. London City are right there, too, and Spurs, with six wins from 11 games so far, are gamely pressing their own case.
What made Sunday's win and performance from Tottenham even more impressive is how dreadful their recent record against Manchester City had been.
Tottenham had lost six of their previous seven away matches against City in all competitions, averaging over four goals conceded per defeat.
Last season City won this fixture 5-2 with Khadija Shaw scoring a 13-minute hat-trick, the quickest in WSL history.
Shaw's early goal on Sunday, her 16th in league matches versus Spurs, could easily have started a landslide.
That was expected. City had won each of their past 17 WSL home games, including all 10 in 2026 â until Tottenham tore up the script.
The outcome means Manchester City, beaten at Chelsea in their previous outing, have suffered consecutive league losses for the first time since January 2025.
'We have maybe been naive - I own that'
Tottenham's victory came down to Ho's brave tactics and his team's superb execution of them.
After going behind, they pressed City constantly, forcing errors and creating chances. That tenacity won them countless one-on-ones, with City unable or unwilling to play over the press.
After her goal, Shaw was rendered anonymous by the hard work and close marking of centre-backs Toko Koga and Amanda Nilden.
Down the right, Kirsty Hanson dominated Carlotta Wamser, could have been awarded a penalty and provided the low cross for Cathinka Tandberg's equaliser.

In midfield, Drew Spence pulled all the strings and covered the entire pitch. At 34, she is perhaps playing the best football of her career and deserved her assist for the winner. After Matilda Vinberg put Spurs in front, several players ran to celebrate with Spence.
"When you come into this, you wonder if it will go against you, but the players were outstanding," said Ho.
"We haven't won here in so long, so we know it will be a tough game, but I have belief in my team when we are on song. I thought we were outstanding - we worked every blade of grass."
Spurs are clearly capable of taking the game to anyone in the league and have now scored 28 WSL goals this season, with only Chelsea and London City having more.
In the second half they adapted to City sending on such fluid attacking threats as Mary Fowler, Kerstin Casperij and Beth Mead.
They lifted the gas from the press, applying it more sparingly, and were solid in defence.

It shows that Ho has learned painful lessons from the past - whether from Spurs' poor record against City, including two five-goal losses in 2025-26, or conceding six to Chelsea and London City back to back in October.
"We have maybe been naive at times and I own that, so we are more reserved," Ho said of his tactical approach. "It was managing that, and the players' communication was excellent."

City were limited to fleeting chances. Jade Rose blasting over after keeper Lize Kop parried a Lauren Hemp free-kick was as close as they came to a second goal, and those were their first shots after a 50-minute drought.
When Spurs got their late chances through the hard work of Vinberg, they could strike for three points.
Vinberg had quite the rollercoaster afternoon. She was initially named on the bench but was promoted to the starting XI 15 minutes before kick-off as Olivia Holdt was suffering stomach cramps.
Perhaps unprepared, she gave away the ball playing out of defence leading to City's opener. But she grew into the game, scored Spurs' second goal and set up Jess Naz for the third.
It was a great moment for Naz, on her 100th WSL appearance of a career that has been disrupted by injury.
Spurs are back in Manchester before Christmas, visiting United on 20 December.
There will be real hope of a positive result as they press their way into contention for what would be a historic achievement of a top-three finish.

articles.headline: Liverpool v Manchester United: Premier League – live
keyFacts: Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United for his first match away against Liverpool at Anfield.
Pochettino urged his 19th-placed Manchester United side to show bravery and have no fear against fifth-placed Liverpool.
Manchester United made three changes to their starting lineup, including the returns of Matthijs de Ligt and Lisandro Martinez.
body: 2 min I bloody knew that team graphic was a lie. United have started with Dalot at right-back and Martinez at left-back. I think. I’ll get back to you because Barcola – playing on the right – has just had a shot deflected behind for a corner.

“Ever since the appointment was announced, I’ve had the words ‘New Manager Bounce’ careering around my brain,” writes Liverpool fan Matt Dony. “It won’t be a surprise to hear I’m not confident. This United side is clearly not brilliant. They’re not as good as they looked at the end of last season, but they’re also probably not as bad as the table implies at the moment. Man for man, they’re certainly not as good as this Liverpool team. And I thoroughly expect them to finish substantially below Liverpool. And yet, today, a new start, enthusiasm, excitement, I thoroughly expect United to look better than they have since before summer. Typical.”
This match is Mauricio Pochettino’s first away game in 35. His USA team had 34 home games in a row (because of the World Cup, and because Haiti away the other day was switched to Miami).

There are two sides to every glory. For every winner there must be at least one loser and the contrast between the two has rarely been as neat as with Manchester United’s Class of 92 and Liverpool’s Spice Boys. They were so different as to make chalk and cheese seem like the perfect sandwich filling. One is a brand, the other a cautionary tale. One maximised their talent; the other pissed their talent up the wall and wore white suits at Wembley. One chose success, the other excess. One claimed a load of leagues and cups, the other collected female trophies. If you count Premier League medals won by the two sets of players, the final score was Manchester United 50-0 Liverpool.

That is how the story is told and, while it does contain an essential truth about the fundamental differences between the sides, it is also a little simplistic. The undeniable greatness of the Class of 92 needs little further exploration, but the story of that Liverpool side is more complex than the received wisdom would suggest. There are multiple interpretations of that era, one of which is that most of the players and the manager Roy Evans should be allowed to embrace and celebrate some of the happiest memories of their life without them being compromised by the phrase ‘Spice Boys’. Robbie Fowler certainly thinks so. In his autobiography he said, “What were incredible times at Anfield – successful, exciting, breathless seasons when I played probably the best football of my career – are dismissed with contempt by those two tiny words.”

This is not to suggest they were blameless. Pretty much all the players acknowledge that, as Fowler puts it, “things happened and they shouldn’t have.” At times they behaved like prats, at times they behaved like another pr- word. There were occasions when it seemed the club anthem had changed to “You’ll Never Drink Alone”. “Win, draw or lose, first to the bar for booze,” was the dressing-room mantra, according to Neil Ruddock. But in the mid-1990s, when the confused celebration of Cool Britannia was at its peak and hedonism was briefly a national pastime, such behaviour scarcely put them in a minority. Nostalgia accentuates the positive in almost everything, yet the Spice Boys are still the subject of ridicule and disdain, seen as laddish underachievers who shamed a proud institution.

The team lost too many important games and in four full seasons under Evans won only the 1994-95 League Cup. The question is whether they won almost nothing because of their reprehensible behaviour or whether their behaviour became reprehensible because they won almost nothing.

They were certainly good enough to outplay the best teams in England. They were the better side in their first five Premier League visits to Old Trafford, yet won none of them. One of those was the 2-2 draw at Old Trafford in October 1995; the Guardian’s Scott Murray said the match “explained 1990s football in a nutshell”, such was Liverpool’s inability to earn a result that was commensurate with their performance. It is a surprise that, for two teams with the perfect combination of attacking ability and mutual distaste, there was no great match between the Class of 92 and the Spice Boys. The 1996 FA Cup final was a notorious stinker. The 2-2 draw earlier that season, a multi-layered minor classic, was the best they produced.

Mauricio Pochettino celebrated his 50th birthday in style. It was March 2022, he was in charge at Paris Saint-Germain and the venue was a stunning boutique hotel; the kind that many capitals have but only Paris truly does. Pochettino’s family and friends were there. So were his inner coaching circle, who are basically family. There were lots of people from PSG. And a good time was had by all.

For Pochettino, it was emotional. As everybody knows, the new Manchester United head coach is the kind of guy to well up when the speeches start, so imagine how he felt when he looked up at the big screen and a video montage of well-wishers started to roll.

Pochettino’s PSG players were at the party. There was no need for anything from them. But there were loads from those he had coached at his previous clubs: Espanyol, Southampton and Tottenham. One by one, the faces flashed up; too many to mention. And, of course, there were the jokes about how old he was getting. But the tone was of pure affection; appreciation, too. Some of the players laid it on thick. They could not help it. They know what Pochettino has done for them.
This is what total buy-in looks like and this is how Pochettino gets you when he finds out which buttons to press.
We are ready. We’ve been working so hard and now it’s about going there to play.

[On the team selection] That is my first starting XI. From today to the next game, you will ask me about changes. I don’t know who played the last game – we assessed the squad from the day we arrive and we believe it’s the best team for today.
[When asked whether United will play three at the back or four at the back, Pochettino bursts out laughing?]You will discover during the game.

“Rob ‘Bob’ Smyth, as I live and breathe,” writes Ian Copestake. “Glad this game is in such .... hands. I will miss it, though. I am in the city as I need a break from looking after mother, and I don’t need this stress/catharsis. What I need is a curry, so damn the lot of youse.”

“Not sure if ‘free hit’ is how I would describe today – United are one spot off stone dead last,” writes Dave Eastheby. “Unless the bar for a good season has been lowered to recent Tottenham levels of ‘not getting relegated’, surely every game from now till May is a must-win or at the very least a must-not-lose.

“Nothing that happens this afternoon will have any real bearing on Pochettino himself but if Utd get a hiding the already-fragile dressing room morale will be non-existent going into Xmas and things will surely get worse before they get better. They need to come away with something today.”
I agree with you about the perils of a hiding, though I still think it’s broadly a free hit for Pochettino – certainly in comparison to most of United’s Anfield trips.
The club offered me a new contract so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on.

We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but because of the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.
The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.
“I think it’s a back five for United, with Dorgu & Dalot being wing-backs,” writes Karen Asad. “It might not be such a bad idea to grind out a result by any means necessary.”
The official team graphic says it’s 4-2-3-1, but lying has become so normalised that it could be a big fat one.

Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation.

Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager.

With hindsight, Michael Carrick’s dismissal was probably inevitable from the moment Manchester United lost at Hull on the opening weekend, just as Ruben Amorim was doomed from the moment cameras picked him up fiddling with magnetic counters on a tactics board in the rain at Grimsby. The message for Mauricio Pochettino is clear: don’t go playing badly on the east coast.

It’s generally acknowledged that Carrick, while he may not have been the ideal manager for United, was a long way down the list of the biggest problems at the club. So what was the point of sacking him? As Pochettino begins his United career at Anfield on Sunday, what realistically can any manager hope to achieve?

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to have “no fear” when they travel to Anfield for his first game. The Argentinian does not want his players to take a backward step as he targets a fast start.

United are 19th in the Premier League and Liverpool fifth but the head coach will not accept any self-doubt. Pochettino is known for being attack-minded and is keen to instil those ideals, but will have had only three days with the players since replacing Michael Carrick.

“We are going to Anfield with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United,” Pochettino told the club’s website. “The history talks for us, and what we need to expect. We need to be sure that we are brave and we are protagonists and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.”

No big surprises in Mauricio Pochettino’s first Man Utd XI. The most notable selection is probably the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt (starting his first Premier League game since November 2025) and Lisandro Martinez.
There are three changes from the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in Michael Carrick’s final game: De Ligt, Martinez and Patrick Dorgu replace Noussair Mazraoui, Harry Maguire and Amad Diallo.
Liverpool bring in Rio Ngumoha for Cody Gakpo, the only change from their win at Crystal Palace before the international break.

The first day in a new job is supposed to be gentle and relaxed: small talk, smaller admin, a few bits of work and some lamentably awkward handshakes. Mauricio Pochettino’s first day* as Manchester United manager is the polar opposite. Liverpool away, the ultimate domestic challenge for any United manager.

This quirk of employment opportunity and fixture list might be a good thing for Pochettino. It’s a free hit, with nobody of sound mind expecting his brave new world to begin until he has had months on the training ground. And if United do win, it’ll increase the length of the free pass that every new manager receives.
Andoni Iraola only joined Liverpool in June, yet he’s already their 11th longest-serving manager. Iraola has made a promising start, including some rousing victories in Europe in particular.

In the Premier League, Liverpool’s main problem has been their home form. They’ve taken five points from five games, but it’s a bit early to lament the demise of Fortress Anfield. Three of those five matches were against the top three of Manchester City, Arsenal and Brighton.
Today, almost unbelievably, Liverpool are playing the team in 19th place: Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United.
Kick off 4.30pm.
* Yes, yes, I know this isn’t actually his first day in the job, but you know exactly what I mean so let’s not allow semantics to undermine a perfectly half-arsed preamble.

The 22-year-old was unavailable for the win over Sheffield United on November 7.
However, manager Nathan Jones confirmed after the trip to Wolves that Leaburn had injured himself in his first training session back.
It added to an existing knee injury for Micah Mbick to further deplete Charlton’s centre-forward options.
Charlie Kelman ultimately led the line for the Addicks before being replaced by Matty Godden during the second half.
Leaburn’s freak injury
Speaking to BBC London post-match, Jones explained: “(Leaburn) Kicked his own foot, opened up his own foot and then had stitches in his foot.
“You couldn’t write it, but it’s the frustrating levels we have. He comes back from the concussion and then in his first training session, which is unopposed, he lacerated his own foot.”
Fortunately for Charlton, Leaburn is expected to be fit to face Lincoln City at home on Tuesday.
Jones added: “We expect him to be back for Tuesday. The frustrating thing is, he’s been out for three weeks, he’s missed two games.
“One from concussion neither him nor us can even remember having and then when he does come back and is adhering to all the protocols, he lacerates his own foot. You couldn’t write it really.”
Charlton are hopeful Leaburn can return to action in midweek Shutterstock Editorial
Leaburn has made 14 Championship appearances for the Addicks so far this term.
However, the academy graduate has yet to open his scoring account in the league.
Instead, his last goal came against Swansea City on the final day of last season.
Charlton setback
In his absence, Charlton succumbed to a 2-1 defeat to Wolves, their fifth loss in six matches.
Godden scored late on for the visitors, who had fallen behind early in the second half.
Quickfire goals from Adam Armstrong and Rafiki Said proved to be enough to claim all three points for Wolves.
Jones’ side have lost five of their last six matches following their defeat at Wolves Getty
The result leaves Jones’ side 19th in the table after 16 matches.
They sit six points clear of the relegation zone ahead of their midweek visit from Lincoln.

articles.headline: 4 random apps you might not realize work with Android Auto
keyFacts: Android Auto supports various productivity, navigation, EV charging, and messaging apps beyond basic streaming and maps.
Meeting apps like Google Meet and Microsoft Teams allow drivers to join audio-only calls from their car displays.
Compatible apps automatically appear on the Android Auto launcher after users install them from the Google Play Store.
body: 4 random apps you might not realize work with Android Auto
Some of these apps will be familiar, while others you may not have heard of.

Android Auto users typically utilize just a few basic apps like Google Maps for directions and Spotify for music. They don't dive into the developer menu; they don't make any serious changes to the way Android Auto works; and they don't know they could be spending all those minutes waiting for someone in a parking lot playing games directly on the car's infotainment display. But the platform's compatible app library runs much deeper, well beyond navigation and streaming.

Android Auto actually supports a surprising range of communication and meeting tools, like WhatsApp and Google Meet, and even a bunch of other apps to help you navigate more efficiently. Each one adds layer after layer of functionality that most users never think to explore. Discovering new apps can genuinely change how you commute while also making it possible to enjoy your drive just a tiny bit more.
Take your work on the road with Google Meet

Android Auto comes with some extra functionality for those in the corporate world, as several popular apps come with Android Auto support for meetings and calls, with Google Meet leading the way. Because Meet is Google's own app, it fits naturally into the Android Auto experience. You can see your upcoming meetings on the car display and join a call with a single tap, all in audio-only mode so your eyes stay on the road. Whether it's a short check-in with your manager or a longer team call, Meet makes it easy to keep up with your schedule even if you have to drive around.

Google's app isn't the only option, though. Zoom, Webex by Cisco and Microsoft Teams all work on Android Auto, offering users the opportunity to join video conferences with audio only. Some apps take integration a step further. Microsoft Teams, for instance, lets users check their calendar and place calls directly from the car display. Google Meet also displays upcoming meetings on your schedule. These features are particularly useful if you're often traveling from location to location but still have to participate in meetings along the way. They also help if you have to leave early to pick up the kids from school while a meeting is still on your calendar.

One thing to mention about these apps is that, depending on your employer, restrictions may apply. Certain companies require corporate apps like Google Meet and Microsoft Teams to run inside an isolated Android Work Profile. In such situations, Android Auto may block calendar sync or prevent the app from appearing on the screen. There's a Work Mode in the works on Android Auto, though, so it may soon be easier to reach all those apps that are locked out by your employer.
Stay fueled up with Fuelio

With gas prices being what they are these days, it's more important than ever to know where to fuel up. Apps like Fuelio can help with that when you're looking for a place to put gas in your car without breaking the bank. Fuelio tracks fill-ups, odometer readings and fuel prices, then calculates your average fuel economy and cost per mile over time. You can even use various filters to display gas stations that were updated within the past day, or those that are most appreciated by users.

Google Maps and other similar tools can surface the nearest gas stations and even tell you the latest prices, but Fuelio gives more in-depth information regarding fuel type, distance and more. Plus, when you throw in all the other features, it's a much better fit if you want to know exactly how much your car is costing you. While Fuelio is free to use with Android Auto, there is a premium version available that costs money.
Stay charged up with PlugShare

If you're driving an EV, then the app you absolutely must use through Android Auto is PlugShare. This free tool (the paid version removes ads) gives you access to a crowd-sourced map that lets you see the nearest charging stations along your route. Its real strength is the community behind it, because drivers leave real-time feedback, uploading photos of the charger layout, reporting broken plugs and checking in after charging. That gives you a clear picture of what to expect before you pull in, so a station that looks fine on paper but has been out of service for days won't catch you off guard.

There are loads of filters you can play with, letting you choose the exact plug type, charging speed and network. You can also check which amenities are nearby, such as restrooms or a place to grab coffee while you wait. It's also a great tool for long-distance drives, as it automatically recommends charging stops along the way based on your specific EV model's range. That goes a long way toward easing the range anxiety that comes with getting an electric car. The one downside is that the data is only as good as its contributors, so stations in less-traveled areas may have fewer recent reports.
Go offline without losing your way with HERE WeGo

Data can be expensive, especially if you use your phone a ton. When you're traveling abroad, costs go up by quite a bit, so you should make the most of your home Wi-Fi. Apps like HERE WeGo through Android Auto offer offline navigation, so your data plan isn't ever a concern. HERE WeGo lets you download maps for entire countries so you always know where you're going. For some countries, you can download maps for certain areas, such as for Germany where you can grab a map for Berlin and another for Hamburg. In the United States, you can grab maps for entire states, but not separate cities.

There are plenty of features to fiddle with to make this app yours, like choosing which fuel type your car uses, having the metric vs. imperial system displayed the way you prefer and so on. The app will flag parking spots and rest areas along the route, and you can even tell it what types of things to avoid. For instance, Waze lets you avoid ferries and highways, but HERE WeGo can have you avoid tunnels and U-turns too. The app can take things one step further and even use visual references on route, which means it will tell you to make a right at the traffic light or when you reach a certain landmark.
Bonus: Get more out of messaging

Yes, Android Auto will read out your texts — we all know that. But it can also handle other apps, reading out your messages if you so desire and then letting you use your voice to reply. WhatsApp is the clearest example of this working well, as Android Auto can read your messages aloud. Then, Gemini asks if you want to reply and will type out the words for you. Signal offers similar read-aloud and reply functionality; so do Facebook Messenger, Microsoft Teams and Google Chat, to name a few.

This feature can be super useful when you're driving as you can stay connected without taking your eyes off the road. The ability to reply to messages will also help you stay on top of any emergencies without having to pull over. However, as with any AI typing tool, you should expect some mistakes here and there.

Adding all these apps is straightforward as you only have to install them from the Google Play Store on your phone. Compatible apps will automatically pop up on your Android Auto launcher. You can go into the Android Auto settings and reorganize the apps if you want to make some more easily accessible. Android Auto's compatibility list is wider than most people assume, but the best setup prioritizes the tools that you actually use when you're behind the wheel.

articles.headline: GTA 6's strong and silent Jason was inspired by Steve McQueen and former Army Rangers, says Rockstar
keyFacts: Rockstar senior vice president Rupert Humphries said GTA 6 character Jason Duval was inspired by Steve McQueen and former Army Rangers.
Game writer Michael Wiafe said Florida crime stories inspired the characters, who are criminals that remain complex human beings.
GTA 6 launched on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies.
body: If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers.

Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway," Humphries said. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite."

That approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves."
Game writer Michael Wiafe said Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly.

"From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them."

Fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it."

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

articles.headline: As cars go digital, US consumers pay an extra $12 billion a year for repairs
keyFacts: Car repair costs for Americans increase by $12 billion annually due to vehicle software fees, according to a report by PIRG.
PIRG said software fees force independent shops to send customers to authorized dealerships, which increases auto insurance premiums for all drivers.
PIRG called on legislators to cap software fees and mandate standardized access to vehicle diagnostic data for independent mechanics.
body: The computerization of cars comes at a price to US consumers, according to the Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), which says that software fees and other charges faced by mechanics push up garage costs.

An investigation by the non-profit consumer group estimates that car repair costs for Americans have been inflated by $12 billion each year, as vehicles integrate more computerized functions. Its report, Closing Shop , is available online.

To find a failed sensor, release an electronic parking brake, or perform diagnostics, a technician has to first connect a laptop or tablet to the vehicle. To so this, the repair shop has to have the right software tools, and that means paying the vehicle manufacturer subscription charges and other fees, in order to get the information they need to complete the job.

If smaller independent repair shops can’t afford all the necessary software or subscriptions, they may be forced to steer customers to authorized dealerships for some fixes – about one in five jobs – and this allows the latter to charge more.

PIRG claims that drivers pay for this through their insurance premiums, even if they never need to get their car fixed, because higher repair costs mean higher insurance claims. It says the price of auto insurance has risen three times as fast as the rest of the US economy since 2012.

Even if mechanics do choose to pay for the software, they spend an estimated collective 83 million hours a year buying, downloading, logging in, and waiting. At typical repair rates, that adds up to $12 billion.

A separate report from the PIRG Education Fund claims that a two-tiered repair model now exists, where independent sites conduct repairs with less information, less powerful diagnostic tools, and higher associated costs than the authorized dealerships.

The advocacy group wants to see legislators take this issue in hand, and has a number of recommendations for them. One is to stop manufacturers from locking out independent mechanics from simple repair jobs like changing brake pads, and require them to support a standard protocol for authenticating independent diagnostic tools.

Another is to give owners control over their vehicle’s data via a standardized platform for accessing telematics repair information, so that the owner can give access to an independent repair shop. Car firms can use the vehicle data to tell owners that a repair is needed and to take it to an approved repair shop, without even disclosing what the issue is.

DIY repairers should be able to get everything they need to fix their own cars. Service information and basic diagnostic software should be free, and PIRG also wants a cap on the license fees manufacturers charge for their official software tools.
“We’ve allowed car manufacturers to build a toll road between the mechanic and the repair,” says Nathan Proctor, leader of PIRG’s Right to Repair campaign and co-author on the report.

“We have a plethora of tolls on the road – subscriptions you need for manuals, diagnostic tools, secure access and more. Not only are all these tolls expensive, they also create traffic jams, slowing down the whole process, which adds to the costs for consumers.” ®

articles.headline: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port likely caused by drone attack, officials say
keyFacts: An explosion occurred on a Russian ship at Benghazi port following a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government said.
Libya's Tripoli-based government warned against hosting foreign forces, citing risks of involving national facilities in external conflicts.
Libyan authorities are investigating the explosion and coordinating with Russian counterparts to determine who is responsible.
body: - Published
An explosion has occurred on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base port after a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.
The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libyan state media reported, citing the eastern government.
It added that the site was secured, and there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.

Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC, reviewed by BBC Verify, shows a boat on fire at 0547 GMT at the Benghazi port, with a separate image captured several hours later appearing to show the same vessel partially submerged.
Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship engulfed in flames and smoke, while it is still dark.
The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) said the Russian ship was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.
Sunday's incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.
GNS said the country was not party to the Russia-Ukraine war, or any other conflict beyond its borders.

Seperately, Libya's internationally recognised government in Tripoli - the Government of National Unity (GNU) - warned against hosting foreign forces and allowing them to use facilities in a statement published by state media.

GNU said such activity raises "serious fears" about "risks that may result from involving ports and civilian facilities in activities related to external conflicts, and the resulting threat to the lives of citizens and the safety of national facilities and assets".
Libya fractured into violence and instability after its leader Muammar Gaddafi was overthrown in 2011, leading to the opposing governments.

articles.headline: Zelensky renews pressure on US to provide patriot missiles after latest Russian drone strike
keyFacts: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called on the United States to supply Patriot missiles following a series of Russian drone and missile strikes.
Zelensky said Russia launched thousands of drones, bombs, and missiles over a week, damaging a five-story apartment building.
Zelensky urged the U.S. to authorize missile transfers under the PURL program and deliver 100 Patriot missiles monthly for winter support.
body: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky is calling for the United States to send patriot missiles to his country after the latest barrage of Russian airstrike attacks.

Zelensky’s call comes just weeks after the State Department officially agreed to sell 500 patriot missiles to the country after shipments were delayed because the U.S. was working with a limited interceptor stockpile. The missiles comes as part of the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List, or PURL, agreement in which NATO funds U.S. made defense equipment for Ukraine.

Zelensky posted on Sunday about the latest Russian drone attack on Ukrainian soil, saying the drones took out a five-story apartment building, leaving 14 people unaccounted for while nine were evacuated. He said the attack capped off a week in which Russia used 2,700 drones, nearly 1,460 aerial bombs, and 165 missiles, including North Korean missiles, and then renewed the call for more help from the U.S.

“Against this backdrop, it is particularly difficult to understand the delays in supplying anti-ballistic interceptors to Ukraine,” Zelensky said in a statement. “We need to strengthen our defense. It is very important that America authorize the transfer of missiles for Patriot systems that our partners have already paid for under PURL. It is also important to continue contributions to the PURL program, which is our main source of anti-ballistic interceptors.”

The State Department authorized the sale of $2.1 billion worth of missiles to Ukraine at the end of October. The department added that despite the initial delay in sales due to the limited stockpile, “no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a result of this proposed sale.”

“This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe,” the State Department said.
POLAND INVESTIGATING SUSPECTED RUSSIAN VIOLATION OF AIRSPACE, DEFENSE MINISTER SAYS

Zelensky called the approval a “strong decision” by the State Department, but ripped the fact that the missile could begin arriving in “ONLY IN A FEW YEARS.” He called for a supplemental “winter support package” that would designate a transfer of 100 Patriot missiles each month from the U.S. to Ukraine.

Zelensky’s continued call on Sunday for more patriot missiles also follows President Donald Trump’s meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping , during which Trump called Putin a “friend.”

articles.headline: Rockstar says GTA 6's mission design allowed opportunities ‘we have never had before to inject dialogue into the open-world experience to bind it together with the story being told’ — ‘This is the most seamless experience we have achieved in a game’
keyFacts: Rockstar Games developers said Grand Theft Auto 6 was designed to seamlessly blur the lines between missions and open-world gameplay.
Vice president Stephen Donkin stated that playing with two protagonists allowed deeper story integration within the open world.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is out now for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S, TechRadar reported.
body: - Rockstar Games has explained why Grand Theft Auto 6's intricate mission design for two protagonists was "a huge challenge"
- Vice president of design Stephen Donkin says, "We worked really hard on this game to blur the lines between 'on-Mission' and 'off-Mission' and even between types of 'Mission'"

- Senior design director for missions and visualization, Luke Howard, adds that Rockstar "strove to approach our Missions this time with more openness than before and better align the player’s agency with our characters"
According to Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto 6's intricate mission design for two protagonists was "a huge challenge," but its ambition allowed it to achieve something it's never done before.

"We worked really hard on this game to blur the lines between 'on-Mission' and 'off-Mission' and even between types of 'Mission'," said vice president of design Stephen Donkin in a series of developer notes sent to TechRadar Gaming.

GTA 6 is a massive game that can take an incredible amount of time to explore, and players will find not only a narrative focused on Lucia and Jason, but also ways their decisions will impact the open-world around them.

Donkin explained that the game has "a lot of different content types running under the hood" and "often at the same time." Rockstar hopes the player doesn’t see these missions as "types" and "just lets the game work its magic on them and present a wide array of things happening all the time, wherever they are."

"Having the ability to be able to play in the open world with your partner was a huge challenge, but it has allowed us opportunities we have never had before to inject dialogue into the open-world experience to bind it together with the story being told more than ever throughout all ways the player chooses to play," Donkin added.

Senior design director for missions and visualization, Luke Howard, echoed Donkin, saying, "This is the most seamless experience we have achieved in a game," and unlike anything players are used to, even from Red Dead Redemption 2, which paved the way for the intricate systems featured in GTA 6.

"Building on the techniques we’ve developed in our previous games to pull the player in and out of Missions, we strove to approach our Missions this time with more openness than before and better align the player’s agency with our characters’ — which has allowed the player more room to play while recognizing the narrative goal they need to achieve," Howard said.

"Combined with the pure range of mission types and our open-world systems, the hope is the player finds themselves fully invested in Jason and Lucia’s story, and however they play that on- or off-Mission becomes intrinsic to that experience."

articles.headline: This '90s-inspired horror game has one of the coolest post-apocalyptic worlds I've ever seen
keyFacts: Players navigate a camper van in the demo for the 2D horror game The Road of Dust and Sorrow, protecting a young daughter from infected humans.
Developer Painted Black Games states they drew inspiration from horror series like Silent Hill and Resident Evil for the title.
The game features smooth gunplay, intuitive puzzles, and a pixel-art post-apocalyptic world that combines creepy aesthetics with a cozy camper van home.
body: I often find myself thinking where the best place to survive a zombie apocalypse would be. A walled-off stone house would certainly make for some good defenses, a boat would be great—but only if the zombies didn't pull a Fear the Walking Dead—or you could spend the end of the world in a camper van. That would certainly be whimsical.

You do just this in The Road of Dust and Sorrow's demo, although it's certainly not as whimsical as I first imagined it to be. You see, in this 2D horror game you have bigger responsibilities than just keeping yourself alive, you also have a young daughter to look out for as well.

This isn't an easy task. Supplies are dwindling, zombie-like humans infected by addictive chemicals amble across the land in search of more dust, but they'll settle for your blood instead. Plus there's this creepy Pastor who's definitely up to something very bad. I only got one glimpse of him in the demo and he was surrounded by a lot of gore and eldritch horror, so I've just decided that staying away from him is probably for the best.

But you can't hunker down and forget about all these terrors, because you have a daughter to feed and protect. So I spent most of my time in the demo gathering food, medical supplies, and trying to locate an item that may just grant us safe passage to the only sanctuary humanity has left.

The dev, Painted Black Games, says it took inspiration from horror series like Silent Hill and Resident Evil for The Road of Dust and Sorrow, and while I haven't come across anything particularly traumatic in a Silent Hill sense yet (although I wouldn't be surprised to see that here) I can see the through line to Resident Evil.

The action is smooth, accurate, and rewarding—which surprised me as I usually don't vibe with 2D gunplay, sometimes the controls are too finicky, but it certainly works here. Head-shotting the zombies is incredibly satisfying, as is kicking them to the floor and beating them with a baseball bat.

Then there are the puzzles. I didn't come across too many, but the ones I did find were very rewarding. It's not rocket science, but the solutions aren't always obvious either. They are, however, very intuitive; you can do a lot with a little, something I very much appreciate.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

But my favourite aspect of The Road of Dust and Sorrow has to be just how cool this post-apocalyptic world is. Maybe it's the pixel art, but it manages to look dilapidated and creepy while also being oddly pretty to look at. I was searching an abandoned warehouse full of zombies and rotting cargo while thinking to myself that with a bit of elbow grease this place could really scrub up.

If you want pretty and cosy, though, the campervan is where it's at. I didn't spend as much time as I would have liked to there, but it managed to feel like a real home—the only safe place left in this world.

Elie is a news writer with an unhealthy love of horror games—even though their greatest fear is being chased. When they're not screaming or hiding, there's a good chance you'll find them testing their metal in metroidvanias or just admiring their Pokemon TCG collection. Elie has previously worked at TechRadar Gaming as a staff writer and studied at JOMEC in International Journalism and Documentaries – spending their free time filming short docs about Smash Bros. or any indie game that crossed their path.

articles.headline: Progressives unveil $25 minimum wage push to solve affordability crisis despite economist inflation warning
keyFacts: House Democrats unveiled a proposal to raise the federal minimum wage from $7.25 to $25 an hour.
Economist E.J. Antoni warned the hike could drive up unemployment, while progressive lawmakers stated it helps workers afford living costs.
Progressives plan to advance the proposal as part of the Democratic economic agenda in the 120th Congress.
body: House Democrats are pushing to raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour, calling the current hourly pay a "remnant of slavery" to "oppress women," despite warnings from conservative economists that the proposal could drive up costs and threaten jobs.

The proposal from the Congressional Progressive Caucus would more than triple the current $7.25 federal minimum wage, raising questions about its potential impact on businesses and workers in states with significantly lower living costs than major cities.

"We should be rallying around (a minimum wage of) $25 at minimum, and it should be cost adjusted for inflation , so that people can have a job that enables them to survive and thrive," Rep. Everton Blair Jr., D-Ga., told Fox News Digital.
AOC-BACKED $25 MINIMUM WAGE PLAN SOUNDS GREAT — BUT AT WHAT COST?
Asked whether a nationwide $25 minimum wage could hurt workers and businesses in lower-cost states, Blair argued that the proposed rate should serve as a national baseline.
The congressman said $25 an hour should be "the floor" and "should be higher in places with a higher cost of living."
Blair acknowledged concerns that raising the minimum wage could contribute to inflation but said lawmakers must find a way to increase workers' earnings while "keeping people afloat."
Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., echoed Blair's support for the proposal, pointing to the high cost of living in cities such as Seattle and Washington, D.C., as justification for raising wages.
DEMOCRATS SEIZE ON MIDTERM WINS TO PUSH MASSIVE MINIMUM WAGE HIKES, BUT ECONOMISTS SEE TROUBLE AHEAD
"The truth is that the boogeyman, the corporations, don't want to pay their workers liveable wages," Ramirez told Fox News Digital.

Heritage Foundation chief economist E.J. Antoni warned that a $25 federal minimum wage could increase costs and unemployment, arguing that the economic consequences would extend beyond major metropolitan areas.
"Whenever a price floor on labor is set above the market equilibrium, a surplus of labor is created. In this case, we call that surplus unemployment," Antoni told Fox News Digital.
DEMOCRATS PLOT MASSIVE SPENDING SPREE AFTER MIDTERM ROUT — AND TRUMP COULD HELP THEM PULL IT OFF

Despite those warnings, progressive lawmakers expressed confidence that the proposal could gain support from Democratic leadership in both chambers and potentially reach President Donald Trump's desk.
"There's a widespread coalition of folks in the Democratic caucus who have long been saying that one job should be enough to pay the bill," Blair told Fox News Digital.
Ramirez also expressed cautious optimism about the possibility of Trump signing the legislation, pointing to his previous willingness to discuss bipartisan immigration reform.
She said she "never knows what the president might or might not be willing to do."
SANDERS-AOC BACKED PROGRESSIVE DEBUTS FEDERAL $25 MINIMUM WAGE BILL WITH COALITION OF 100+ ORGANIZATIONS
The Living Wage for All coalition , which joined lawmakers in unveiling the proposal, says support for a $25 minimum wage extends beyond Democratic voters.

"Not a blue wave," the coalition said, citing polling it claimed showed 63% of Republicans support a $25 federal minimum wage. "There is a blue collar demand that says that this is how we address the affordability crisis."

Coalition members also drew comparisons between the history of minimum-wage policies and slavery-era labor practices, arguing that the current wage system has historically disadvantaged women and marginalized workers.

The proposal comes as Democrats prepare to advance their affordability agenda in the 120th Congress, with progressives seeking to make higher wages a central component of the party's economic platform.
Neither House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries , D-N.Y., nor the White House responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

articles.headline: U.N. climate summit ends without deal after contentious fossil fuel debate
keyFacts: The U.N. COP31 climate summit in Turkey ended without an agreement due to disputes over phasing out fossil fuels.
Delegates from nearly 200 countries failed to reach consensus after the European Union rejected drafts omitting fossil fuel language.
Turkey's environmental minister confirmed no deal was adopted because summit rules require unanimous agreement among all participating parties.
body: COP31, the United Nations', ended Sunday without a final agreement after days of contentious talks collapsed, mainly because of disputes between nations pushing to phase out fossil fuel use and others opposed to doing so.

The breakdown capped two weeks of negotiations in Antalya, Turkey, between delegations from nearly 200 countries. Their debates ran into overtime, becoming the longest COP summit in history, at a moment that U.N. officials and many scientists have called decisive for the trajectory of global warming and climate change.
U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres said in a statement that Sunday he was "deeply disappointed" by the outcome of the summit.

"I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," he said. "But this setback does not change the facts. There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science."

The United States sent no representatives to the climate conference, following the Trump administration's withdrawal from the 2015 Paris Agreement. That accord set a goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above preindustrial levels, a target that has anchored every U.N. climate summit since and that the world is now poised to overshoot.
Talks reached an impasse Sunday, as the European Union opposed a draft agreement that failed to mention fossil fuels and which, its delegates argued, placated countries that export them.

"We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuel, which is the key driver of climate change," said Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU in Antalya. "And we will not accept negotiating backward in time, and we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel."

The EU joined a group of smaller nations facing heightened threats of climate extremes and challenged oil producers, like Saudi Arabia, that staunchly rejected their views. The finale came after days of tense discussions over some of the core topics at issue during the summit, including whether to establish new rules and goals around transitioning away from coal, oil and natural gas in favor of renewable energy.

COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is Turkey's environmental minister, said in televised comments from Antalya on Sunday that a draft had not been adopted due to a lack of consensus. The conference rules require unanimous agreement to reach a deal, so even a single nation's dissent can derail the process.

"We have always emphasized that this process is one that respects the will of the parties. We did everything we could," Kurum said. "In the end, we did not impose this text on anyone. We did not pressure anyone with a take-it-or-leave-it approach. There are parties in the hall that oppose this text, and we see that there is no agreement on it. Therefore, these decisions have not been adopted."

Australia's climate and energy minister Chris Bowen, who shared the COP31 presidency with Kurum as Turkey and Australia jointly hosted this year's summit, said Sunday that talks broke down because of "unbridgeable red lines" and added that "the situation coming into this COP was the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory," reported CBS partner BBC News.

On Friday, the scheduled final day of the conference, a coalition led by France and Panama and including countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific rejected the latest draft agreement as too weak, according to the U.N. The group demanded explicit language on fossil fuels and stronger commitments on climate finance.

"We cannot continue to be held hostage by petroleum producers," said Panama's environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, at a news conference last week. He also vowed that Panama would formally object to any deal omitting issues related to fossil fuels.

An initial draft of negotiators' agreement had called for "accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels," a recurring goal at these summits, and urged an end to inefficient fossil fuel subsidies. It also resolved to bring warming back below 1.5 degrees as early as possible this century. But that language was gone days later, reflecting deep divisions over timelines and financing.

Later drafts still did not contain language about fossil fuels, although they did include proposed targets to capture billions of tons of carbon dioxide annually from the atmosphere by 2035, using technology that critics have said distracts from the need to cut fossil fuel use. They also called for electricity to supply more than a third of the world's energy by the same deadline, alongside goals around renewable energy and energy efficiency.

Negotiators had expressed "deep concern" in drafted text over global warming, which at its peak is projected to exceed 1.5 degrees. They also reaffirmed the need "for deep, rapid and sustained emissions reductions," warning that every increment of additional warming will increase the frequency and intensity of climate-related loss and damage. If current international climate plans were fully implemented, they noted, the world would be on track for just over 2.5 degrees of warming, down from projections of more than 4 degrees before the Paris accord.
The COP31 summit unfolded in a year marked by,, destructive wildfires, and other anomalies, which meteorologists have largely tied to. Scientists say its effects are amplified by climate change.

Speaking in Antalya last week, Guterres urged governments to move away from fossil fuels, triple adaptation funding by 2035 and tax fossil fuel companies' windfall profits to help vulnerable nations recover from disasters. "Polluters must pay," he said. At a press conference two days later, he linked the climate crisis to deeper social and political instability.

"You cannot eradicate poverty when climate disasters keep throwing people back into it," Guterres said. "You cannot promise young people a better future while destroying the natural systems on which that future depends. And you cannot speak seriously about justice when those who did least to cause the crisis suffer first and worst."
Some environmental advocates felt the conference proposals didn't go far enough to meet the needs of communities that are already facing real consequences of the climate crisis.

Ellen Dorsey, named this month to the TIME100 climate list, told CBS News after leaving Antalya over the weekend that she hadn't expected substantial action from COP31, despite clear signs of urgency.

"The time for simply talking about phasing out fossil fuels is over. Governments need to act," Dorsey told CBS News. "That means no fossil fuel expansion, an end to fossil fuel subsidies, and an equitable phaseout that protects workers and communities."

Dorsey said fossil fuel lobbying has grown over the past decade, as has the presence of industry interests in national delegations at U.N. climate talks, including this one. Still, she sees promise in efforts pushing back, from grassroots movements to the Santa Marta process, a coalition using diplomacy to drive a transition away from coal, oil and gas.
"Momentum is building beyond the negotiations," said Dorsey, who called this "a historic inflection point" for climate policy. "The opportunity for real systemic change is here."

articles.headline: UN climate talks break down over bitter disagreements on fossil fuels
keyFacts: UN climate talks in Turkey failed to reach an overarching agreement after delegates clashed over whether to explicitly mention fossil fuels.
The European Union and several nations rejected a draft omitting fossil fuels, while Russia and Saudi Arabia pushed to exclude them.
Australian negotiator Chris Bowen said the previous international agreement calling for a transition away from fossil fuels remains in force.
body: ANTALYA, Turkey (AP) — Chaotic United Nations climate talks in Turkey couldn’t reach an overarching agreement on Sunday because of disagreements over whether to mention the fossil fuels that cause global warming.

Expectations had already been low heading into the two-week negotiations, but discussions about explicitly including fossil fuels — the chief cause of global warming — and other issues, including money, proved irreconcilable.

The talks, called COP31, continued without a main agreement known as a cover decision. The meeting had already made progress on smaller issues that nibbled at the process and the warming problem and continued to go on after the failure on the cover decision.

Any pact approved at the talks has to be by a near-unanimous consensus. Several countries and the 27-nation European Union said they couldn’t accept the final proposal from the joint Turkish-Australian leadership that didn’t mention fossil fuels.

A considerably larger number of nations said that consensus on something was more important and accepted the decision, often reluctantly. Russia and Saudi Arabia pushed to keep fossil fuels out of the document.

Darragh O’Brien, minister of climate, energy and the environment of Ireland, onscreen, speaks during a closing plenary session as COP31 President Murat Kurum, sits center, at the COP31 U.N. Climate Summit, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, in Antalya, Turkey. (AP Photo)

“It’s unconscionable that we would have a climate act that makes no reference to fossil fuels,” Irish Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said on behalf of the EU at the climate talks, which ran nearly 48 hours overtime at the Turkish resort town of Antalya.
For most of the first 25 years of the United Nations climate talks, outcomes didn’t explicitly mention fossil fuels, until three years ago.

That’s when, in the oil-rich United Arab Emirates, a groundbreaking agreement called for “transitioning away from fossil fuels,” but since then there’s been no explicit mention of fossil fuels. The Turkish-Australian proposal recalled the Dubai deal entirely, but that wasn’t enough for many nations and environmental groups.

Adding to the disagreement was the fact that the draft included explicit language and a goal for carbon capture and storage for industrial polluters, which many nations and activists said would run against efforts to reduce overall emissions.

“The failure of this COP to deliver ambitious, fair, science-based outcomes falls squarely on the shoulders of richer nations, petrostates, and the disgracefully incompetent duo of the Turkish and Australian COP presidents,” said Rachel Cleetus of the Union of Concerned Scientists.
COP31 President Murat Kurum, center, leaves a closing plenary session at the COP31 U.N. Climate Summit, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, in Antalya, Turkey. (AP Photo)

As the proposed deal fell apart in the plenary session, Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum, the president of COP31, was absent, leaving it to Elchin Allahverdiyev of Azerbaijan to announce the failure.
JOE CONCHA: AS TRUMP AND VANCE SPLIT, THE NOMINATION IS RUBIO’S TO LOSE

“Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision. And that’s disappointing, very disappointing,” said Australia’s Chris Bowen, the president of negotiations in the unusual joint leadership.

Bowen said the explicit call in the Dubai agreement to wean away from coal, oil and natural gas that cause climate change is still in force: “Transition away from fossil fuels in the real world is happening. It’s happening. It’s happening at speed and it’s irreversible.”

articles.headline: Can we build a more ethical AI future?
keyFacts: Marc Lamont Hill speaks with tech entrepreneur Anil Dash on UpFront about artificial intelligence risks and the need for greater industry accountability.
Recent developments raising industry stability questions include Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, widespread technology outages, and hacked European refrigerators.
Anthropic began trading publicly at a two trillion dollar valuation amid growing concerns over AI economic risks, privacy, layoffs, and environmental impact.
body: Marc Lamont Hill speaks with tech entrepreneur Anil Dash about AI’s risks and the fight for ethical technology.

The artificial intelligence boom is transforming the global economy and concentrating enormous power in the hands of a few technology companies. But a series of developments is raising new questions about the industry’s stability and accountability from the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy to a wave of technology outages affecting the US government, major banks, companies and aviation systems alongside reports of hacked refrigerators across Europe. Concerns are mounting over the economic risks, mass layoffs, privacy and environmental impact of AI. And as AI company Anthropic began trading publicly, reaching a $2 trillion valuation, questions are mounting over whether the extraordinary levels of AI investment are sustainable. Is there a future where AI can be used for the collective good?

This week on UpFront, Marc Lamont Hill speaks with Anil Dash, former adviser to the White House Office of Digital Strategy in former United States President Barack Obama’s administration, about the risks of the AI boom, Silicon Valley’s growing political influence and the urgent need for greater accountability.

articles.headline: Iran taunts Trump, shows off underground ‘missile city’ with new double launcher

body: Iran unveiled a new underground missile launcher capable of firing two rockets simultaneously, releasing footage of the weapon in what appeared to be a warning to President Trump as Washington weighs renewed military strikes against Tehran.
The launcher is designed to fire two liquid-fueled missiles at once, marking the first time Iran has publicly displayed the new system.

Liquid-fueled missiles offer operators greater flexibility to adjust their speed and flight trajectories, while the launcher’s underground location could make the weapons more difficult for US and Israeli forces to detect and destroy.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps aerospace force previously demonstrated a launcher capable of simultaneously firing two solid-fueled missiles on April 7. Sunday’s footage, however, showcased the country’s newly developed liquid-fuel system.

Maj. Gen. Ahmad Vahidi, the IRGC’s commander-in-chief, visited the facility and received briefings on the force’s combat readiness and recent missile developments.
“We have integrated ‘surprises’ and highly effective assets into our combat structure,” Mousavi said.
Footage showed Mousavi riding through the underground tunnels in a Jeep as military personnel displayed an extensive collection of missiles and launch equipment.

The video also featured a handwritten message aimed at the White House, declaring: “At the White House, being a b—–d isn’t an insult; it’s a qualification standard.”

The display appears intended to counter Washington’s claims that Iran’s missile program has been severely weakened by the conflict and to signal that Tehran retains weapons capable of threatening US and allied forces.
Trump has repeatedly touted the military campaign as a major success, declaring a “very big victory” and describing the war as “effectively over.”
“We’re just keeping it the status quo,” Trump told reporters at the White House earlier this month, while warning that the US remained “locked and loaded” if circumstances changed.

The president also directed Vice President JD Vance to halt negotiations with Iran over its nuclear program.
But the possibility of renewed military action remains on the table.

Trump is reportedly weighing a four-to-seven-day bombing campaign against Iran alongside Israel, according to reports from The New York Times and Axios, following new intelligence about Tehran’s efforts to rebuild its missile capabilities.

The reports came after Roman Gofman, the director of Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency, traveled to Washington and reportedly pressured US officials to consider another round of strikes.
Israel has also warned the White House that Iran is making advances in its chemical and biological weapons programs.
Any renewed American offensive would likely focus on Iran’s missile arsenal, though energy infrastructure and other military facilities could also be targeted.
Among the missiles displayed were the Fattah, which Tehran claims is a hypersonic weapon, and the long-range Khorramshahr missile.
Some weapons in the footage were deliberately blurred, apparently to conceal details of Iran’s remaining military capabilities.

The underground facilities could complicate any future US or Israeli campaign by providing protected storage and launch locations for weapons that may have survived previous strikes.

body: Members of the opposition Congress party protested outside Meta’s offices in Delhi on Friday and appear to have entered the building in a video shared by CNN. Members of the party’s youth wing are demanding the company restore accounts of party leaders and warned of more protests to come. The Congress party has criticized Meta for censoring speech that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his BJP party disagree with, and has placed banners accusing Mark Zuckerberg of favoring BJP around the city.
Protesters storm Meta offices in India
Members of the youth wing of the Congress party are demanding its leaders’ Instagram accounts be reinstated.

While two accounts in question were restored Friday, Manu Jain, who oversees social media for the party’s youth wing, told Reuters that “thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted.”

In February, India issued tighter rules around the removal of “unlawful” content, changing the timeline from 36 hours to just three.
